group: insects: Drosophilidae wings (Houle et al. 2017 Nature: 117 species, 21,138 species wings, 17,323 G-matrix wings, 12,075 M-matrix wings; 12 landmarks)

data.landmarks: Houle D, Bolstad GH, van der Linde K, Hansen TF 2017 Nature 548:447-450; Zenodo 4999258 (`NatureDryad.zip`: `SpeciesNature.csv` 12 2D wing vein landmarks across 21,138 wings from 117 Drosophilidae species, plus `AllAlignedNature.csv` with 17,323 additive genetic Gw wings and 12,075 mutational M wings).
data.phylogeny: Open Tree of Life induced subtree (`datasets/thompson/drosophilidae/opentree_induced_subtree.json`, 88 matched species with Grafen branch lengths).

what_thompson_specifically_adds: Houle et al. (2017) famously showed that spontaneous mutation (M) and standing genetic variance (G) predict 40 Myr of drosophilid wing evolution (D). Applying Thompson's 7-mode basis tests whether (1) drosophilid wing venation has a higher Thompson-7 variance share than Hymenoptera wings (~40%) because the 12 landmarks span a simpler dipteran vein grid, and (2) mutational (M) and genetic (G) covariance matrices channel macroevolutionary divergence (D) preferentially along the 7 global Thompson coordinate modes.

hypotheses.statement: Across the 117 drosophilid species means (12 2D landmarks), the 7 a-priori Thompson coordinate modes capture > 50% of between-species Procrustes variance (exceeding the 38.8% hornet and 42.2% bee forewing benchmarks).
hypotheses.reasoning: With 12 landmarks (20 Procrustes DOF vs 32-34 in Hymenoptera), 7 smooth coordinate modes span a larger fraction of shape space and capture the primary proximal-distal radio-medial vein shifts.

hypotheses.statement: Interior crossvein landmarks (the 4 middle landmarks along the proximal-distal axis) have a higher unexplained residual fraction after Thompson-7 than the 8 proximal/apical margin landmarks.
hypotheses.reasoning: In both hornets and bees, interior crossvein intersections shifted locally relative to the global wing outline; dipteran anterior/posterior crossveins should show the same local residual concentration.

hypotheses.statement: Phylogenetic signal on the 88-species OpenTree topology: best multivariate evolutionary model in full PCA-95% space is NOT White Noise (Pagel's lambda > 0.3).
hypotheses.reasoning: With 88 species across Drosophilidae, subgeneric and species-group clustering on the OpenTree topology is much better resolved than the 30-species Vespa polytomy.

hypotheses.statement: Leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction in full shape space beats the grand consensus (median Procrustes RMS ratio < 0.95, paired one-sided Wilcoxon p < 0.01).
hypotheses.reasoning: Matches the 0.75 subjective prior registered for `drosophilidae_wings` in `thompson_dataset_portfolio.json`.

hypotheses.statement: Mutational-macroevolutionary alignment (Houle M vs D): in the 20-PC space of `AllAlignedNature.csv`, the leading axis of spontaneous mutational variance (M, n=12,075) and standing genetic variance (Gw, n=17,323) both align strongly with between-species macroevolutionary divergence (D, n=21,138), with |cos theta| > 0.50.
hypotheses.reasoning: Direct check of Houle et al.'s (2017) core finding that mutational and genetic lines of least resistance align with macroevolutionary divergence.
